title: Salade de Pommes de Terre
subtitle: French potato salad dressed with mustard vinaigrette and shallots
excerpt: Waxy potatoes dressed warm with a sharp Dijon and white wine vinegar dressing, shallots and flat-leaf parsley. No mayonnaise. Serve at room temperature alongside cold meats or fish.
sourceNotes: Classic French bistro accompaniment; dressing applied while the potatoes are warm so they absorb it fully.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 hours ahead. Add the parsley just before serving so it stays bright.

content.text: This French potato salad uses a mustard and vinegar dressing instead of mayonnaise. Dress the potatoes while they are still warm so the dressing soaks in. Do not let them cool completely before adding the vinaigrette or they will stay dry in the centre.
Cook the potatoes in a large pan of salted boiling water for 18 to 20 minutes. They should be tender when pierced with a knife but not falling apart.
While the potatoes cook, whisk the Dijon mustard, white wine vinegar, salt and pepper together in a large bowl. Whisk in the olive oil until the dressing comes together.
Drain the potatoes well. Leave them to steam dry for 2 minutes in the colander.
While still warm, cut any large potatoes in half. Add all the potatoes to the bowl with the dressing.
Add the sliced shallot. Toss gently so the potatoes are coated in the dressing. Leave to sit for 15 minutes.
Scatter over the chopped parsley just before serving. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

items.symptom: The dressing sits on the surface and does not soak in.
items.cause: The potatoes were too cold when dressed.
items.fix: Always dress while the potatoes are warm. The starch opens up and pulls the dressing inside.

items.symptom: The shallots taste sharp and raw.
items.cause: The shallots were sliced too thickly, or they were added too late.
items.fix: Slice very thinly and add at the same time as the warm potatoes so they soften slightly.

items.cause: The potatoes were not salted during cooking.
items.fix: Salt the cooking water generously. Potatoes absorb very little seasoning from a dressing alone.
